title: Architecting Power Platform for Complex Enterprise Solutions with Ian Tweedie [MVP]
description:
Power Platform solutions often start as quick low-code apps and end up business-critical, integrated and hard to maintain. In this interview Ian Tweedie explains to Power Platform makers, developers and architects how modular features, server-side logic, Key Vault, Git-based ALM and intent-based governance keep enterprise solutions maintainable.
In this episode
00:00 – Intro: when low-code becomes enterprise02:28 – Ian's path to Power Platform08:14 – Breaking solutions into features and modules20:14 – Just enough architecture for citizen developers30:21 – AI, MCP and modular design40:57 – Secrets, Key Vault and environment variables46:03 – Git, ALM and source control51:24 – Governance, the architecture playbook and rapid-fire
Key takeaways
Low-code is not no-code: once Power Platform solutions become business-critical, classic clean-architecture principles such as single-purpose, decoupled features apply just as in pro-code.Business-critical logic should run server side, and secrets belong in a governed store such as Azure Key Vault rather than in reversible places like environment variables.Governance works best when it defines intent and lets makers show how they meet it, while source control in Power Platform always means choosing the least-worst option.
Worth quoting
“if it's something that has to be right and always must be accurate then we need to execute that server side” – Ian Tweedie (07:44)
“If we're storing it in a place that's reversible then we potentially shouldn't be storing it there unless it's somewhere like key vault where it's got the right governance around it.” – Ian Tweedie (41:04)
